article.title: Acusativo y genitivo con verbos negados: ejemplos
article.chapter: Acusativo y animacidad — Винительный падеж и одушевлённость

claims.summary: Cornell states that some verbs normally taking accusative require genitive when negated, while some allow either accusative or genitive.
The example contrasts genitive рюмок with accusative рюмки and gives лук/лука as equivalent under negation.
The three listed negative examples reproduce the forms and case contrast on Cornell’s page.
The article restricts its statement to the examples explicitly described and avoids broader semantic rules.

locator.description: Cornell, “Genitive object with a negated verb,” lines 0–5: some verbs require genitive when negated; рюмки (acc.)/рюмок (gen.); лук/лука alternatives said to have the same meaning.

links.notes: Article is narrowed to the two patterns and examples in the consulted passage.
